correctness.rationale: For nonadjacent a,b sharing w, any v in N(a) but not N(b) gives a countervaluation with p true only at b: Δp holds at a and v but fails at w. Therefore distance-two vertices have equal neighborhoods, ruling out geodesics of length at least three and making nonadjacency with equality an equivalence relation within components. Conversely, in a bipartite complete component the neighbors of a vertex all have the same successor set. With ≥3 parts, if p is constant on the neighbors of a vertex in A, each of those neighbors sees all of A and some vertices of that common exterior value; all neighbors therefore agree on Δp. Isolates satisfy the schema vacuously. In a complete multipartite component the only bridges occur in stars; deleting a nonbridge must make its endpoints equal-neighborhood nonneighbors, which requires two singleton parts. Inserting internally splits a two-element part, and inserting between components creates a bridge and hence must form a star. These give precisely the marked edit locations, with both endpoints counted for K₂. The component series x+B−e^x counts one isolate type and set partitions into at least two parts; marking a singleton pair or a center and leaf of a larger star gives D. For an independent insertion-side derivation, two marked isolates and a marked size-two part in a nontrivial component give x²/2+(x²/2)(B−1); attaching an isolate to a designated star center gives x[x²+x(e^x−1−x)]. The sum equals D, and each is multiplied by H for the rest of the components. A fresh exhaustive semantics/location check over orders 0–5 and a separate exact coefficient recurrence through the displayed ranges reproduced both sequences.
residual_risks: The independent replay tests semantics and every edit through n=5, not all orders; the universal proof supplies the latter. n=0 is an enumeration convention, not a nonempty frame.
